patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 6-week history of tingling pain in the sole of his right foot, which worsens when he raises it above chest level during exercises. He mentions that he began exercising regularly 2 months ago and experiences right calf cramps with the use of the treadmill's incline feature, necessitating frequent breaks. The pain subsides completely after a few minutes of resting. He adds an 8-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot upon elevation

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Smokes two packs of cigarettes daily for 34 years.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with tingling pain in the sole of the right foot, especially upon elevation and during exercise, with a significant history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and smoking.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello—what brings you in today? Patient: For about six weeks I’ve had tingling pain in the sole of my right foot, especially when I raise it above chest level during exercises. When I rest for a few minutes it goes away completely, but I also get right calf cramps when I use the treadmill incline, so I have to stop often.
This sounds like it could be related to blood flow or

Patient: It does seem tied to activity—if I keep exercising with my foot raised, the tingling starts up, and my calf will cramp, but after I sit and rest for a few minutes the symptoms clear completely. I’ve also had type 2 diabetes for about eight years, and I smoke heavily.
Have you noticed any changes in the color or temperature of your right foot compared to the left, or any sores on your foot or toes that aren't healing?
“Yes—my right foot sometimes feels a bit cooler than the left, and I’ve noticed it looks slightly paler. I don’t have any obvious sores or wounds, and nothing has failed to heal.”
Have you ever experienced pain in your right foot or toes while lying flat in bed at night that wakes you up or requires you to hang your foot off the edge of the bed for relief?

Patient: Yes, sometimes at night I get pain and tingling in that right foot that wakes me up, and hanging my foot off the bed for a bit helps. It isn’t constant every night, but it does happen enough to affect my sleep.
Have you noticed any hair loss on your right leg
Patient: Yes, I think there’s less hair on my right lower leg than on the left.

Patient: “Yes, I’ve had less hair on my right lower leg than the left, and the foot does feel cooler and paler at times. I also get night tingling and pain that wakes me up, and when I let my foot hang off the bed for a few minutes it improves. I’m hoping we can figure out what’s causing it and whether it’s affecting the blood flow to my foot.”
[DDX] Peripheral arterial disease, Critical limb ischemia
